BILL NUMBER:  S3653

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to establishing
minimum distances in which a refiner may operate a retail service
station; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :

To establish the minimum distance in which a refiner may operate a
retail service station.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Amends section 199-a of the general business law by adding
a new subdivision 6 which adds the definition of "Refiner".

Section 2. Amends the general business law by adding a new section
199-o.

1. Distance limitations

(a) cities with a population greater than or equal to 1 million = 1
mile

(b) counties with a population greater than 900,000 not wholly
contained within a city = 1.5 miles

(c) all other counties = 2 miles

2. Exceptions to distance limitations where:

a) divided highway

b) natural physical barrier

c) located on Indian tribe

3. Arbitration

4. The effect of this legislation may not he modified or disclaimed by
contract or agreement and may not be contradicted by evidence of any
prior usage or by a prior course of dealing or usage of trade.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The bill attempts to promote price competition, which will ultimately
provide a balance in retail prices. Consolidation of major oil
companies taken, together with direct operation of retail locations by
major oil companies, has constricted competition. The bill strives to
preserve a competitive marketplace in which independent dealers,
franchisees and distributors are able to survive.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.3941, 2007-2008; S.6636, 2005-06; S.4428-B, 2003-04.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be deemed
repealed three years after such effective date; provided, however,
that the Provisions of this act shall not apply to; (a) retail service
stations operated by a refiner with company personnel employed by such
refiner or employed by a parent company of such refiner where the
refiner retains ownership of the motor fuel or with any person, firm
or corporation managing a retail service station on a commission fee
arrangement under contract with the refiner where the refiner retains
ownership of the motor fuel on the effective date of this act; (b) any
retail service stations for which a refiner has applied for a building
permit prior to the effective date of this act and for which
construction commences within 90 days after the effective date of this
act; and (c) any retail service stations acquired by a refiner in a
single transaction involving the purchase often or more retail service
stations and which are operated by a refiner with company personnel,
employed by such refiner within 90 days after the effective date of
this act.

summary: Establishes various minimum distance requirements for operation of a retail service station by a crude oil refiner; provides for certain exemptions and for arbitration of disputes arising therefrom.
title: Establishes the minimum distance in which a refiner may operate a retail service station
